assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new materials platform: a tunable flat-band system with correlated insulators and superconductivity that was predicted and then realized in devices. As an experimentalist in materials and nanostructures I value a clear, original discovery with a decisive measurement and a large body of follow-on work across physics and materials science.
assessment.attribution: The continuum-model flat-band prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the 2018 transport discovery (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators) are distinct, decisive contributions that fit a compact configuration. Andrei's earlier STM and spectroscopic work on twisted layers is relevant, and the allocation among theory and experiment is the main open question.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups with several measurement techniques including scanning probes, and now a mature field. Recognition is timely, though the superconducting mechanism is still debated.
uncertainties: Credit split between Bistritzer-MacDonald theory and the experimental discovery, and the proper role of Andrei and others who observed early twist-dependent signatures.
Mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled; the prize rationale would need to rest on the flat bands and correlated states.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators established a new classification of electronic phases with protected edge and surface states. The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental realization are original, clear, and have had lasting impact on materials research.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical framework, and Molenkamp's group delivered the HgTe quantum spin Hall measurement following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. I propose Kane and Molenkamp as the theory and experiment pair; Mele, Zhang, Hasan and Xue make a three-person limit hard and credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent experiments including ARPES and transport, and well established for roughly two decades; the prize is plausibly timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution among theory (Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Fu) and experiment (Molenkamp, Hasan, Xue); the exact configuration is unresolved.
Only the supplied names can be proposed here, so this entry omits some who may deserve credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength proposal and realized with strontium and other atoms, reached fractional uncertainties in the 10^-18 range and opened precision tests of fundamental physics and geodesy. It is a clear invention with a concrete, measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye's group drove the clocks to record accuracy and stability; both are decisive and fit a two-person prize. Others contributed to related clock work, such as ion clocks, which are partly recognized already.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related prizes (Hall and Haensch 2005, Wineland 2012) could be viewed as incremental by some members.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the history of the magic-wavelength proposal and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the crystalline MgO junction turned spin-dependent tunneling into the basis of hard-disk read heads and magnetic memory. It is a materials-engineering discovery and invention with enormous practical reach, in which control of interfaces and crystalline quality is decisive, which I recognize from microscopy-based interface studies.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, while Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated the large MgO(001) effect in 2004 with a theoretical precursor in Butler and Mathon. Four credited names and a theory contribution outside the list make a three-person selection difficult.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and commercially deployed for years. The area is mature, but a spintronics prize followed GMR (2007), which weighs on timing.
uncertainties: Dropping Miyazaki is a judgment call, as the 1995 discovery was reported by two groups.
Whether the committee views this as a continuation of the GMR prize rather than a separate discovery is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus sensor and CO-functionalized tips brought atomic force microscopy to sub-molecular resolution, imaging bond structure and charge distributions. It is a genuine instrument invention with a clear discovery, extending the lineage of scanning probe prizes. My background in electron microscopy makes me weigh instrument-driven progress but also hold it to the test of whether it has changed physics rather than technique.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor, while Gross, Meyer and collaborators demonstrated the functionalized-tip imaging of molecules. The list supports a three-person division of instrument and application.
assessment.maturity: Adopted widely and reproduced in many laboratories; the field is mature. Recognition of imaging techniques is reasonable, but the impact is mostly in surface science and chemistry.
uncertainties: The conceptual breadth of impact for physics is narrower than for the top candidates.
Priority between Giessibl, the IBM group and others on functionalized tips is not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-gain X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond, coherent, tunable X-ray pulses and enable structural and dynamic studies in materials, chemistry and biology. As the 2023 cycle recognized attosecond light for probing electron dynamics, a source that probes matter at the atomic scale and in time has comparable standing as an enabling invention.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini and Kim contributed core SASE theory and design; Rossbach was central to FLASH and the European XFEL. The decisive experimental demonstration of LCLS lasing involved people who are not among the credited names, so the supplied credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several facilities operate and the science output is large. Timely; the discovery is an accomplished accelerator-physics achievement.
uncertainties: Credited names omit key figures in the LCLS realization, so a fair configuration may not be reachable from this list.
It may be seen as a facility and engineering achievement more than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site microscopy, provides a clean experimental route to many-body physics. It is a substantial and original field, though its core discoveries are spread over several contributions.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposals, and Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger delivered the key experiments. Five credited names exceed three, and I pick one theorist and two experimentalists, which leaves out equally strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and mature, though practical quantum advantage for simulation is still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution is unavoidably wide and any three-person choice is contestable.
The impact on open physics problems is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero theta13 closed a missing piece of the three-neutrino mixing picture and enabled searches for CP violation. It is a clear, decisive discovery with lasting consequence.
assessment.attribution: The reactor measurement by Daya Bay was reported in parallel with RENO and Double Chooz, with T2K providing accelerator evidence. Luk and Wang led Daya Bay, but the credit among collaborations is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several experiments and now precise, so it is mature. A neutrino prize was awarded in 2015 and 2002, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and parallel results make a fair two- or three-person configuration difficult.
Outside my own field of expertise, so my assessment relies on general knowledge.
